item.title: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Director’s Next Movie Officially Picked up by Sony
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: [Filtered: Anime adaptation news; Naruto is explicitly toss content.] Sony and Lionsgate are teaming up for Spider-Man Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton's live-action Naruto movie
item.content:encoded: The live-action Naruto movie is officially moving forward, thanks to some help from Sony. The anime adaptation from Destin Daniel Cretton (Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Short Term 12) has been in the works at Lionsgate and is now set to begin production next year. This marks yet another collaboration between Cretton and Sony, a partnership that saw massive success this year with the latest Tom Holland Spider-Man movie.

item.title: Jason Statham and Guy Ritchie Officially Reunite for New Action-Thriller
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.description: [Filtered: Generic action-thriller streaming announcement without prestige substance.] Netflix brings Jason Statham and Guy Ritchie back together for another action-packed revenge flick, Dogfight.
item.content:encoded: Guy Ritchie and Jason Statham have worked together numerous times over the years, bringing us fun, action-packed flicks. The duo will soon be doing it again, not only in the upcoming Viva La Madness but also in Netflix's newly announced film, Dogfight.

item.title: Scream Star Confirms She’s Returning for Sequel
item.dc:creator: Elijah Gonzalez
item.description: [Filtered: Casting gossip for generic horror franchise; not prestige horror.] The original scream queen, Neve Campbell, will return for Scream 8.
item.content:encoded: One of the definitive scream queens is coming back for another night with Ghostface. Neve Campbell confirmed she will return as Sidney Prescott (now Evans) in Scream 8.

item.title: Netflix Officially Reveals Blue Eye Samurai Season 2 Premiere Date and Episode Count
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: [Filtered: Anime series renewal; anime content is toss.] Netflix's animated tale of swords and revenge is coming back soon with its second season.
item.content:encoded: The first season of Blue Eye Samuraiended with the perfect teaser for a drastically different season 2. Since then, fans have spent three years waiting for Netflix's animated show to return and pick up where it left off. Thankfully, the long wait is almost over as Netflix has announced the season 2 release date and Mizu's quest for revenge is about to reach new heights.

item.title: 'Avatar: Seven Havens' Season 2 Could Return to 'The Last Airbender’s Most Iconic Location
item.dc:creator: Corey Plante
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV series analysis/speculation; not horror or prestige.] Avatar: Seven Havens’ creators confirmed a faster journey through the remaining Havens, suggesting Pavi could reach New Ba Sing Se in season 2.
item.content:encoded: Ba Sing Se once survived a century-long war by pretending the war didn’t exist at all, only to get taken over by the Fire Nation during Avatar: The Last Airbender. Despite ongoing political turmoil extending through The Legend of Korra’s era, the Earth Kingdom’s former capital persisted — and one version of it even survived the Cataclysm. Avatar: Seven Havens revealed the existence of a Haven called New Ba Sing Se during season 1, offering a glimpse of a society still clinging to old traditions while its people go hungry. And based on one specific detail from the season finale, there’s a very good reason to suspect we'll get to see the city of New Ba Sing Se firsthand in season 2.

item.title: 'The Mandalorian' Meets 'Avatar' in Netflix's New Sci-Fi Western Masterpiece
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Anime-adjacent sci-fi western; anime news falls under toss category.] Bass X Machina puts an anime spin on the story of a legendary lawman
item.content:encoded: Created by LeSean Thomas and Studio Mir, who both worked on The Legend of Korra, Bass X Machina is a reimagining of the story of Bass Reeves (Brian Tyree Henry), an escaped slave who worked in Indian Territory as a deputy U.S. Marshal. Reeves’ real life was extraordinary, and is said to have inspired the character of the Lone Ranger, but Bass X Machina also gives him a cybernetic arm that shoots magic bullets. The criminals he fights get even bigger upgrades, and the stakes can at times escalate to truly ludicrous levels. Henry does an especially great job expressing exasperation as Bass faces plenty of absurd foes, like an outlaw in a rampaging bull mech that requires complex cooperation to take down.

item.title: Zelda Ocarina of Time release time in your time zone
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] The Zelda Ocarina of Time release time is just around the corner. Here's when you can expect Ocarina of Time to launch in your time zone
item.content:encoded: The Zelda Ocarina of Time remake release time is just around the corner, as Nintendo introduces a new generation to one of its classic games. Unlike the 3DS port from 2011, Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 includes a massive visual overhaul, along with several quality-of-life features that weren't present in the original Nintendo 64 release. Pre-orders are still open at some retailers if you're hoping to snag a special bonus, though US-based folks only get one bonus to choose from.

item.title: 20 Years Later, Uncle Iroh's Wisest 'Avatar: The Last Airbender Quote' Is Still Undefeated
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.category: Avatar The Last Airbender: The Quest for Balance
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective ('20 years later'); matches toss pattern.] Uncle Iroh's timeless advice helped shape Zuko's journey, and its message still resonates almost two decades later.
item.content:encoded: Avatar: The Last Airbender has more than its fair share of heartfelt moments and poignant lines. Whether it’s Aang reassuring a downtrodden Toph in the vast loneliness of the desert, or Ursa’s parting words to her son Zuko before disappearing in the middle of the night, the series can be surprisingly deep for what some might (incorrectly) consider a mere children’s show. No character embodies that richness and depth more than Uncle Iroh, who begins as Zuko's wise mentor and becomes so much more. Time and again, Iroh sits at the center of The Last Airbender's most moving moments, offering quiet wisdom just when it's needed most.

item.title: New Star Wars Book Reveals the Surprising '90s Inspiration for an Iconic New Character
item.dc:creator: Aimee Hart
item.description: [Filtered: Star Wars big-franchise churn; art book behind-the-scenes content.] 'The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian' by Phillip Szostak traces the film's evolution from beginning to end — with a shock reveal.
item.content:encoded: After years on Disney Plus, Din Djarin (Pedro Pascal) and his surrogate Jedi son, Grogu, made their big-screen debut in The Mandalorian and Grogu earlier this year. Now, The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu by Phillip Szostak is set to hit shelves this week, offering a behind-the-scenes look at the film’s production from start to finish.

item.title: World of Warcraft Forever release time in your time zone
item.dc:creator: Oli Welsh
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Here's what time World of Warcraft: Forever is set to launch in your time zone.
item.content:encoded: The release of World of Warcraft: Forever brings a third — or, depending on how you count them, a sixth or seventh — way to play World of Warcraft to everyone with a WoW subscription. Joining the modern game and the Classic servers, Forever is based on WoW as it was at launch in 2004, but with new content, rebalanced classes, graphical enhancements, and lots of modernization.

item.title: Daniel Craig's Taut 92-minute Thriller Is Blowing Up on Streaming
item.dc:creator: Sam Hill
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: streaming clickbait headline] Daniel Craig's forgotten psychological thriller is climbing HBO Max's charts, despite earning one of the worst Rotten Tomatoes scores of his career.
item.content:encoded: Daniel Craig has established himself as one of Hollywood's most reliable leading men, particularly when it comes to action movies and suspenseful thrillers. From his gritty breakout role in Layer Cake to the high-stakes mysteries of Knives Out and The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo, Craig has built an impressive filmography outside his best-known role as James Bond.

item.title: FF7 Remake and Rebirth Are Less than $8 Each on Nintendo Switch 2
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: [Filtered: Game sale/discount announcement, not news.] Square Enix's Nintendo eShop sale includes huge discounts for FF7 Remake and FF7 Rebirth on Switch 2, both of which are on sale for under $10 each
item.content:encoded: If you've been waiting for Final Fantasy 7 Remake and Rebirth to go on sale before checking them out, your patience has paid off. At least, as long as you're okay with a bit of DLSS hair-frizz. Square Enix is hosting a huge sale on the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 eShop, and included in that sale are FF7 Remake and FF7 Rebirth for $7.99 and $7.49, respectively.

item.title: Huge Square Enix Sale for Switch 2 Includes 90+ Games At Discounts Up to 85% Off
item.dc:creator: Sam Hill
item.description: [Filtered: Generic sale announcement, filler content.] Square Enix is holding a massive Nintendo Switch 2 sale, with discounts on Final Fantasy, Dragon Quest, Octopath Traveler, and more.
item.content:encoded: Nintendo Switch 2 owners have plenty of great RPGs to choose from, but building up a digital library can get expensive. Fortunately, Square Enix is making that a little easier with a massive Nintendo eShop sale, offering steep discounts on some of its biggest franchises.

item.title: Percy Jackson Season 3 Official Trailer Shows Off Star-Studded New Cast
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: [Filtered: TV show news without prestige or substance.] Percy Jackson and the Olympians shows off Dafne Keen, Ming-Na Wen, and more in latest season 3 trailer
item.content:encoded: With just a few weeks until season 3 of Percy Jackson and the Olympians premieres, Disney has released a stunning new trailer for the next chapter of the Rick Riordan adaptation. Season 3, which will cover the 2007 novel The Titan's Curse, looks to be the darkest entry in the show yet. While the new trailer sets up the stakes of the latest adventure for Percy and friends, it also signals that the end of the road isn't far off.

item.title: Google Is Quietly Hiding A New Zelda: Ocarina of Time Easter Egg
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hernandez
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective/Easter egg filler.] Google celebrates The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time with a time capsule harking back to the 1998 release of the N64 classic.
item.content:encoded: The official release of the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarinaof Time is only a couple of days away, but search engine Google has already started the festivities with a clever nod to Nintendo's landmark adventure game.

item.title: 'Calvin and Hobbes' Best Babysitter Quote Is Still Among the Funniest in Comic Strip History
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip, not game/horror/prestige content.] In Bill Watterson's comic strip Calvin and Hobbes, Calvin's arch-enemy was Rosalyn the babysitter. Here is her best quote ever.
item.content:encoded: Batman has the Joker, Superman has Lex Luthor, Captain America has the Red Skull, and for six-year-old Calvin, his avowed arch-nemesis is Rosalyn, the diabolical babysitter who makes him go to bed at 6:30.

item.title: Luke Skywalker's Single Greatest Star Wars Line Hits Harder Than Any Sci-Fi Quote Since
item.dc:creator: Aimee Hart
item.category: Star Wars: Episode VIII - The Last Jedi
item.description: [Filtered: Star Wars franchise churn; fits 'fans furious' nostalgic analysis pattern.] Luke Skywalker is easily the greatest 'Star Wars' character of all time. But what was his best quote?
item.content:encoded: Since its 2018 debut, Rian Johnson’s The Last Jedi has sparked heated debate over whether it was a fantastic or terrible Star Wars film for Luke Skywalker. Still, whatever your opinion, it’s hard to deny that Johnson’s take on the greatest Jedi ever came with some truly epic quotes. And no, we’re not talking about the zinger, “Amazing. Every word of what you just said was wrong.”

item.title: 10 Best BG3 NPCs Fans Still Want To Join The Party All These Years Later
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Corgan
item.description: [Filtered: List article about game NPCs; fits 'how to/unlock' guide category.] The best BG3 NPCs are still unable to join your Baldur's Gate 3 party, but fans have wanted them to be party members for years.
item.content:encoded: Baldur’s Gate 3is full of moments like this: A great character, an intriguing story, and then no reliable way to learn what happens next. For Mizora — Wyll's patron devil, the one who granted him his warlock powers — a new mod has delivered a way around that issue. While Mizora technically does hang out in camp, she does so only on her terms — and when you see her, generally, you want to shove her back into whatever pocket of the Nine Hells she's crawled out of. Unless, of course, you can recruit her hellish talents to support your aims. Now, thanks to the mod Mizora Joins the Party from modder WorldWalker42, you can do exactly that. She's not the only NPC who deserves an upgrade to companion status. Here are 10 more.

item.title: 10 Best Classic Shooters That Are So Good They Never Need A Remake
item.dc:creator: Chris Guest
item.description: [Filtered: Generic retrospective list of old games, not substantive news or analysis.] The best classic shooters of the 2000s were perfect two decades ago, and don't need a remake in 2026.
item.content:encoded: The 2000s represented a golden age for shooter games. Both first-person and third-person shooters saw a plethora of all-time classics released across a number of platforms during the aughts, while the immense success of consoles such as the PlayStation 2 and 3 and Xbox 360 helped spearhead the genre's push into the mainstream. More than two decades later, many of those games remain standard-bearers for shooters as a whole.

item.title: 8 Years Later, a Buffy Star's Obscure Thriller Is Waiting to Be Discovered on Free Streaming
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective + streaming clickbait, despite horror tag.] Remember, everyone, if you find a strange mask in the woods, don't put it on
item.content:encoded: There was a time in the distant past when good things could occasionally come out of Twitter. Back in 2017, novelists Sam Sykes (the Aeons’ Gate series) and Chuck Wendig (Blackbirds, Star Wars: Aftermath) got on the website currently known as X to co-write an improvised horror satire. The result was a firmly tongue-in-cheek deconstruction of slasher movies, concerning Sykes' unnamed character’s new job as a camp counselor and an unfolding massacre in the woods. The story quickly went viral. (While the tweets are still up, Wendig has since abandoned X and locked his account, so the original story can no longer be read outside of a handful of unofficial screenshot archives.)

item.title: 5 Classic Nintendo Games That Are So Good They Never Need a Remake
item.dc:creator: Jason Venter
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old games, not news or analysis.] Remakes and remasters are all the rage, but five classics from Nintendo are good enough that no one ever needs to bother trying to improve them.
item.content:encoded: Video games have been around for so many decades that the next time you sit down to play one, you’ll have tens of thousands of terrific options to choose from. A lot of us find ourselves playing newer releases when the time rolls around, because older titles have slipped from our minds. But they can also provide ample entertainment, if we give them a chance.

item.title: Pokémon Go 'Halloween 2026 Part 2' event guide
item.dc:creator: Julia Lee
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Here's all the bonuses and perks for Pokémon Go's "Halloween 2026 Part 2" event, which includes the debut of shiny Greavard.

item.title: All map and weapon loot pool changes in the Fortnite Chapter 7 mini season
item.dc:creator: Julia Lee
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] The Fortnite Chapter 7 mini season, "Treasure Hunters," completely changes the map. Here's everything different in the new season.
item.content:encoded: The Fortnite Chapter 7 mini season, titled "Treasure Hunters," puts you on an island with several warring pirate crews. There's new map POIs, weapons, and items waiting as your treasure to claim as characters like Kasane Teto and Monkey D. Luffy make their Fortnite debuts.

item.dc:creator: Julia Lee

item.dc:creator: Julia Lee
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Here's a look at all of the Fortnite Chapter 7 mini season's battle pass skins, and the various styles they come in.
item.content:encoded: Fortnite's Chapter 7 mini season, "Treasure Hunters," has kicked off, bringing a smaller battle pass alongside it (as one would expect from a shorter season). This battle pass is full of goodies, including two outfits featuring characters from One Piece and some anime-styled Fortnite characters.

item.title: 6 Perfect Star Trek Episodes to Watch to Say Goodbye to Patrick Stewart
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV retrospective list, not substantial film/TV news.] “Live now. Make now always the most precious time.”
item.content:encoded: Even more significant than the quantity of Star Trek that Stewart made was the quality. Kirk is in many ways a classic pulp action hero. He faces conflicts head on, never afraid to throw a punch or flirt with a sexy alien. Picard represents a different form of masculinity, valuing compassion, knowledge, and communication above all else. He is the endlessly patient father figure for his crew, and for the next generation of Star Trek viewers, presiding over one of the most beautiful visions of what the future could look like. It’s that connection that has left fans in mourning following his death on Thursday at the age of 86.

item.title: The 10 Most Anticipated Sci-Fi and Fantasy Books of November 2026
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Book promotion list; not games or core Polygon content.] Get cozy with sky pirates, faerie princesses, and political schemes
item.content:encoded: When fall brings cold, windy, and wet weather, it’s the perfect time to stay inside and curl up with a good book. November offers plenty of options, with fresh entries in long-running series, standalones by bestselling authors, and brand-new talent to check out. Whether you want to imagine sailing with sky pirates, exploring a haunted forest, or flirting with faeries, the 10 most anticipated sci-fi and fantasy books of November offer plenty of ways to pass a rainy day.

item.title: 15 Years Ago, Zelda Told its Most Memorable Story with its Worst Gameplay
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Corgan
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword HD
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective (15 years ago); matches toss pattern.] Zelda’s most memorable story still shines, but the motion controls, Fi, and repeat fights often make it a tough replay
item.content:encoded: Hold the controller over your head. The Master Sword glows. Point it at the screen, hit Y to recenter, and swing. On the screen, Link swings… kind of the right way. Then, your chatty companion, Fi, chimes in with a very long and earnest explanation of something you figured out several minutes ago. Rinse and repeat for about 40 hours, and that’s Skyward Sword, one of the most cinematic, heartrending, memorable stories Zelda has ever told — and the one saddled with the most finicky gameplay.

item.title: Netflix's Near-Perfect Thriller With 94% Rotten Tomatoes Score Is Getting Cut From Streaming
item.dc:creator: Debopriyaa Dutta
item.description: [Filtered: Streaming removal clickbait; generic TV news.] Two eccentric teenagers cross paths and embark on a road trip to remember.
item.content:encoded: The End of the F***ing World is among the best in this genre. Based on Charles Forsman’s minicomics, the eight-part miniseries follows James (Alex Lawther), a teen who thinks he is a psychopath, and Alyssa (Jessica Barden), who considers James a welcome distraction from her tumultuous home life.

item.title: 7 Near-Perfect Prime Video Sci-Fi Shows that Hook You in the First Scene
item.dc:creator: Debopriyaa Dutta
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV list; not game or substantive film/TV content.] Sci-fi comes in all flavors, including ones that are addictive.
item.content:encoded: Prime Video is home to sci-fi shows of great variety, but some of the best ones capture our attention from the get-go. When a premise is solid and well-thought-out, the first episode often becomes a promising indicator for the rest of the story. With that in mind, here are seven near-perfect Prime Video sci-fi shows that hook you right from the first scene.

item.title: 6 Perfect 'Peanuts' Comics from the 1960s that Prove Charles Schulz is a Genius
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Graphic-novel/comic strip retrospective; not game-related.] The best decade for Charles Schulz's Peanuts comic strip was the 1960s — here are six perfect comics which prove it.
item.content:encoded: By the 1960s, Schulz hit his sweet spot with well-defined characters and a freshness to the material which would sometimes flag in the decades to come. Don’t get me wrong, there are plenty of hilarious, heartwarming, and inspired Peanuts comics from the ‘70s, ‘80s, and ‘90s, but taken as a whole, nothing tops 1960s Peanuts.

item.title: 20 Years Later, The Departed's Best Line Is Still One Of The Greatest Quotes In Gangster Movie History
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Old movie retrospective opinion; lacks substance.] Jack Nicholson delivered mob cinema's ultimate statement of power.
item.content:encoded: In crime cinema, a lethal line of dialogue can carry just as much weight as a loaded gun. Martin Scorsese's Goodfellas hooks audiences with Henry Hill's seductive declaration, “As far back as I can remember, I always wanted to be a gangster,” framing a life of crime as the ultimate aspiration. Miller's Crossing features Tom Reagan's wonderfully blunt take on underworld survival, while Casino, Scarface, and The Godfather overflow with dialogue that has long since bled into the cultural lexicon. Immortal phrases like “keep your friends close, but your enemies closer” and “an offer you can’t refuse” remain cinematic icons right alongside the actors and directors who brought them to life.

item.title: Forget Jason Statham, the Best Action Movie of the Last 30 Years Is Back on Netflix
item.dc:creator: Corey Plante
item.description: [Filtered: Streaming clickbait; generic action movie promotion.] Get off his plane. Air Force One is streaming on Netflix.
item.content:encoded: Harrison Ford spent decades making wildly implausible heroes feel like ordinary guys having a terrible day. An archaeologist outrunning a giant boulder? Sure. A space smuggler taking on an evil empire? Absolutely. In Air Force One, he pulls off something that now feels considerably more farfetched: an American president you’d trust with your life.

item.title: 24 Years Later, the Funniest Lord of the Rings Movie Quote Is Still a Legendary Fantasy Line
item.dc:creator: Corey Plante
item.category: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
item.description: [Filtered: Old movie retrospective; nostalgia piece without substance.] The Two Towers’ “meat’s back on the menu” quote remains one of Lord of the Rings’ funniest moments — and raises absurd questions about orc dining.
item.content:encoded: Somewhere in Middle-earth, is there a Chili’s that serves orcs? Does an Uruk-hai host greet hungry customers, tell them it’ll be a 20-minute wait, and hand them a menu? Does the kitchen run out of manflesh halfway through the dinner rush? Is halfling served as an appetizer? What precisely is in the Triple Dipper? These are unreasonable questions to ask of an otherwise perfect fantasy epic. Unfortunately, The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers invites every one of them with one line that feels deeply anachronistic.

item.title: 9 Years Later, Jon Bernthal’s Action Series Is a Masterpiece From Start to Finish
item.dc:creator: Collier Jennings
item.description: [Filtered: Big-franchise Marvel churn; generic retrospective about older series.] One batch, two batch, penny and dime
item.content:encoded: Ever since superhero movies and television became popular, fans have debated which actors are the perfect fit for their characters. The debate has escalated over the years, especially when multiple actors have played iconic characters like Superman and Spider-Man. Nine years ago, one of the best actor-to-character pairings came when Jon Bernthal took on Frank Castle in The Punisher. In the process, Bernthal delivered one of the grittiest and most action-packed comic book adaptations in history.

item.title: Ridley Scott's Near-Perfect Sci-Fi Masterpiece is Waiting to Be Rediscovered on Streaming
item.dc:creator: Maria Loreto
item.description: [Filtered: Streaming clickbait: prestige film available on streaming platforms.] One of the best films in Ridley Scott's filmography and a key entry into the sci-fi canon
item.content:encoded: The ‘70s and ‘80s was a major turning point for science fiction. Star Wars revitalized the genre in 1977 and turned it into one of Hollywood’s main box office draws, inspiring a wave of films that reshaped the entire industry. Two years later, Ridley Scott threw down the gauntlet with Alien, taking a big step away from the optimism that had once permeated sci-fi pulp storytelling and instead infusing it with corporate anxiety and untrustworthy artificial intelligence. It was a signal for things to come.

item.title: All 8 Dungeon Crawler Carl Books Ranked (by Their Goodreads Score)
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Graphic novel/book promotion; LitRPG book ranking list.] Matt Dinniman's hit LitRPG series keeps raising the stakes, but which Dungeon Crawler Carl book ranks highest?
item.content:encoded: Matt Dinniman's Dungeon Crawler Carl takes one of fantasy's oldest setups and throws it into a blender with reality television, apocalyptic horror, and video game logic, creating a series that has evolved into one of the biggest breakout hits in modern speculative fiction. The premise is fairly simple, starting with a fight for survival inside an alien-dominated game show that escalates into a sprawling saga of bizarre monsters, convoluted mechanics, and a talking cat with an ego to match.

item.title: Patrick Stewart's Perfect 'Simpsons' Episode Reveals the Beloved Actor's Secret Weapon
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV nostalgia retrospective; Simpsons guest appearance analysis.] Sir Patrick Stewart is being remembered for Star Trek and X-Men, but he was also the perfect guest star on The Simpsons
item.content:encoded: Yesterday, news broke that Sir Patrick Stewart died at age 86. With his background performing Shakespeare and his incredible sense of dignity and gravitas, Stewart is being celebrated primarily for his work as Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation, as well as being the perfect man to portray Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films. But while he was beloved for the dramatic weight he brought to his roles, it's worth acknowledging that the man pulled off some incredibly memorable comedic performances, one of the first was on The Simpsons, where he guest-starred in the season 6 episode, “Homer the Great.”

item.title: Andy Weir's New Time-Travel Sci-fi Thriller Officially Arrives Nov. 5
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Book/audiobook promo without game or horror connection.] The Andy Weir-produced Audible Original story Exoplanet stars Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo.
item.content:encoded: Andy Weir is known for combining humor, hard science fiction, and gripping survival stories in his bestselling novels The Martianand Project Hail Mary, which were both adapted into blockbuster films. He’s sticking to that formula for his next project, a time-travel thriller that will launch on Audible on Nov. 5.

item.title: KPop Demon Hunters Returns In November with Definitive New Release
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: [Filtered: Anime/animation home media release announcement.] Netflix and The Criterion Collection are bringing 2025's animated K-pop hit musical KPop Demon Hunters home with a new 4K physical release.
item.content:encoded: The Criterion Collection announced back in February thatKPop Demon Hunters would be getting a physical release in another victory for the Oscar-winning sensation. Now Criterion has shared new details about the cornucopia of goodies that will come with the physical disc release of Netflix's animated film.

item.title: 'Adolescence' Creator Officially Confirms a Connection Between His Netflix and Apple Shows
item.dc:creator: Aimee Hart
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV renewal/streaming news without substance or horror angle.] 'Adolescence' co-creator Stephen Graham speaks candidly about the thematic parallel between it and Apple's new crime thriller, 'Nocturne.'
item.content:encoded: Co-created by Stephen Graham and Jack Thorne, the 2025 British limited series Adolescence made waves worldwide when it debuted on Netflix. Adolescence explores the immediate fallout from a young boy, Jamie (Owen Cooper), stabbing a girl to death and the radicalization of men online. The series was so well received that a UK government–backed initiative made it free to watch in high schools.

item.title: Peter Jackson's Worst Lord of the Rings Sin Was Forgetting the Story's Fairy Tale Roots
item.dc:creator: Francesco Cacciatore
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective analyzing old movies, not new news.] Peter Jackson's The Hobbit should have taken inspiration from The Princess Bride on how to adapt a fairy tale into a movie.
item.content:encoded: I couldn’t have been more excited for a movie adaptation of J.R.R. Tolkien’s The Hobbit. The story of Bilbo Baggins is my favorite book — I even prefer it to The Lord of the Rings — and I try to read it again every year. By virtue of being less ambitious, The Hobbit lets Tolkien deliver a compact narrative that makes his talent as a worldbuilder and writer shine.

item.title: 12 Years Later, Sofia Coppola's Unmade Epic Fantasy Still Lives Rent Free in My Head
item.dc:creator: Maria Loreto
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about unmade project, not substantive.] Sofia Coppola, it’s not too late to make your dark take on The Little Mermaid
item.content:encoded: The year was 2014. The live-action Disney remake craze had already begun thanks to the success of Tim Burton's Alice in Wonderland, but it hadn’t reached its box office peak. Meanwhile, on the other side of Hollywood, Sofia Coppola was attached to a movie bursting at the seams with possibilities: a live-action The Little Mermaid, not based on the 1998 Disney animated classic, but on the original Hans Christian Andersen fairy tale, where (spoiler alert) the brokenhearted mermaid dies by flinging herself into the ocean and dissolving into sea foam. I can picture Coppola’s compositions clearly in my mind: the mermaid (Elle Fanning) shot in pastel colors, thoughtfully looking out at the horizon. A song by The Strokes or Phoenix plays in the background.

item.title: Logan Paul Just Proved His 'Pokémon' Haters Wrong
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hernandez
item.description: [Filtered: Pokémon TCG retail/personality story, not substantive news.] The YouTube personality and his ongoing Pokémon money-making schemes is still flawed, but Logan Paul's actually into the trading card game.
item.content:encoded: YouTuber Logan Paul has been accused of a lot of things: ruining the Pokémon trading card hobby, clickbait, greed, thoughtlessness. Maybe some of these condemnations are true. A recent revelation by the blonde provocateur has started to convince me that he may not, in fact, be a larper. Actually, I'm starting to believe the boisterous influencer might legitimately like Pokémon.

item.title: 20 Years Later, Rockstar’s Best Game Still Doesn’t Have the Sequel It Deserved
item.dc:creator: Ford James
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective; not a new sequel announcement.] Bully, or Canis Canem Edit, was one of Rockstar's most innovative and unique games, and it's about time we got a sequel.
item.content:encoded: These days, Rockstar Games is one of the most famous developers in the world. That’s primarily thanks to their magnum opus, the Grand Theft Auto series, but also the Red Dead Redemption games, and to a lesser extent, L.A. Noireand the Max Payne series. In just a few short weeks, Grand Theft Auto 6will finally be here, a game that has felt like a distant dream for so long, after delays and a slow trickle of new information. But 20 years ago, Rockstar released one of its most unique games that has hints of the classic GTA formula, and it's a crying shame that there is still no sign of a sequel.

item.title: 60 Years Later, the Best 'Peanuts' Quote of All Time Still Doesn't Get the Credit it Deserves
item.dc:creator: Corey Plante
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip quote.] In addition to being sweet and funny, Charles Schulz's Peanuts comic strip could be profound at time. The best example comes from 1966.
item.content:encoded: One of the best examples comes from a Feb. 3, 1966, comic strip in which Lucy mocks him for volunteering for a school spelling bee. Charlie Brown’s response contains some of the best advice Schulz ever put on the page. Sixty years later, it’s still something we can all stand to remember.
